name: CI

on:
  # `branches-ignore: ["dependabot/**"]` (instead of `branches: ["**"]`)
  # prevents Dependabot's branch-push from racing with the PR-open event.
  # Dependabot PRs still get CI via the `pull_request:` trigger; the push
  # event was producing a duplicate run that survived the concurrency
  # cancellation because `github.ref` is `refs/heads/...` for push and
  # `refs/pull/N/merge` for pull_request.
  push:
    branches-ignore: ["dependabot/**"]
  pull_request:
    # v2.4.4 Phase 7 (QG-5): `develop` joined this list because the
    # integration pull request targets it. Without it a develop-targeted
    # PR ran only commitlint, so the branch head was tested by the push
    # trigger but the MERGE RESULT -- the thing that actually ships --
    # never was. Path filters already keep the added cost bounded.
    branches: ["main", "develop"]

# v2.11.0 Phase 6.5 (QG-v270-2): read-only token by default. No step here
# writes with GITHUB_TOKEN; a job that ever needs to must declare it.
permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # github.head_ref is set on pull_request events; falls back to
  # github.ref on push. This collapses push/pull_request events for the
  # same effective change into one run.
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# v2.0.0 Phase 5: hardware-gated suites and skip flags are listed in
# docs/archive/v2/v2.0/ci-hardware-gates.md (Playwright, GPU video, live STT/TTS,
# patient-tier adapter). v2.1.0 extends that in docs/archive/v2/v2.1/ci-hardware-gates.md
# (Unsloth live train, diffusion layer-streaming OOM rescue). Do not install
# those stacks in this workflow. Phase 6 audit/JSON CLI/budget units run in
# test-ts; desktop vitest (Node 22) covers sidecar IPC; pytest tests/python
# covers diffusion budget.py.

jobs:
  # ── TypeScript ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  lint-ts:
    name: "Lint TypeScript (Node ${{ matrix.node }})"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22.x", "24.x"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - run: npm run lint

  test-ts:
    name: "Test TypeScript (Node ${{ matrix.node }})"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22.x", "24.x"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      # v2.0.0 Phase 2: browser_* tests use InMemoryBrowser HTML fixtures.
      # CI does not install Playwright or download Chromium. Live Chromium is
      # opt-in locally via NEXUS_BROWSER_PLAYWRIGHT=1.
      - run: npm run test -- --reporter=verbose --coverage
        env:
          CI: "true"
      # v1.19.0 Phase 4: desktop picker/settings tests (FRONTEND_MODELS, LFM
      # license chip) live in the desktop workspace. shell-build.yml only
      # runs them on main; develop pushes need this step. Node 22 only so
      # the 24.x matrix does not double the minutes.
      # v2.2.4: the same `npm run test:shell` job covers chatbot-first
      # routing, installed-catalog pickers, compact media, Models catalog
      # tabs, and Hub skills.sync timeout copy. Do not add a live Hub clone.
      # v2.2.5: the same job covers modelAliases, Models overflow/badges/chips,
      # FolderTree row icons + chats-pane pill, Hub catalog latest stubs, and
      # the scanner allowlist. Do not add a live GPU or live Hub clone.
      # v2.2.6: the same job covers studio.session IPC, Image/Video remount
      # hydrate and implicit last-output follow-up, Agents resume hydration,
      # and Chatbot append-then-remount. No live GPU in PR CI.
      # v2.2.7: the same job covers Settings Models context chips
      # (128k / omit-on-null), chat/coding usage on done events,
      # studio persist of visualUnits, ContextUsageBar 79/80 CTA,
      # the composer picker row on Chat/Agents/Images/Videos, and
      # MessageList once-per-day headings plus bubble time/tokens.
      # v2.2.8 Phase 1: chat.send is not a 15s RPC; ping stays 15s; a slow
      # chat fixture never surfaces sidecar response timeout; Ollama tag
      # gemma4:12b marks catalog gemma-4-12b-it-gguf Downloaded. No live GPU
      # in PR CI.
      # v2.2.8 Phase 2: FolderTree collapse is a 56px icon rail (not an empty
      # 24px gutter); Agents rename/delete go through FolderTree; Image/Video
      # history panes share 280px + collapse; confirm-delete is rounded/quiet.
      # v2.2.8 Phase 3: sidebar module nav has a top inset (not flush with the
      # title bar); chat/coding pending orbs use size=bubble (not inline 20px)
      # and are centered; image/video pending stays hero. No thinking-orbs
      # package. No live GPU in PR CI.
      # v2.2.8 Phase 4: Settings Models matches installer sort (family collapse,
      # hideBelowVram, over-budget last); compact cards; Downloaded highlight;
      # QuickModelSwitcher uses that order. No live GPU in PR CI.
      # v2.2.8 Phase 5: Hub apply quarantines high-severity skills and still
      # swaps Active to the fetched tag. test-ts covers NexusHubSyncer planted
      # jailbreak + scanner-crash fail-closed; test:shell covers ipcSkillsClient,
      # hub-catalog CLI, and SkillsSettings copy. Do not clone Hub. No live GPU.
      # v2.2.8 Phase 6: T001-T012 stay in existing jobs. Cargo test (shell-build)
      # covers rpc_timeout_for (chat.send != 15s, ping 15s). test:shell covers
      # Gemma alias Downloaded, FolderTree 56px collapse, Models sort fixture,
      # Hub quarantine apply. test-ts covers NexusHubSyncer quarantine.
      # installer-tests covers catalog_tab_sort + stale 3.12.0 pack refusal.
      # Do not add a live GPU or live Hub clone.
      # v2.2.9 (T014): the same jobs cover the new contracts. test:shell covers
      # composer chrome (recording-only mic indicator, Context flex 3 / picker
      # 30%), meta-above-bubble full-word tokens with no pending meta, the
      # pendingCaptionRotator pill (fixed list, reduced-motion, stable name,
      # no thinking-orbs dependency), studio header render-when-children +
      # Chats copy, composerSessionUsage visual budget, typed diffusion
      # strings through resultGuard/dispatcher, modelPills + catalogTabs
      # downloaded-first + Embeddings-first, hubTags normalize + SkillsSettings
      # staged sync/quarantine copy. test-ts covers catalog visualTokenBudget
      # rows and the PromptInjectionScanner one-pair waiver. pytest (runtimes/)
      # covers the typed CUDA/weights/GPU kinds and pytest-only stub gating.
      # installer-tests covers Embeddings-first TYPE_TABS, name-row fact pills,
      # patient-tier visible + never-recommended, downloaded_first partition.
      # Do not add a live GPU or live Hub clone.
      - name: Desktop vitest (Node 22)
        if: matrix.node == '22.x'
        run: npm run test:shell
        env:
          CI: "true"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        if: always() && matrix.node == '22.x'
        with:
          name: ts-coverage
          path: coverage/
          retention-days: 7

  build-ts:
    name: "Build TypeScript (Node ${{ matrix.node }})"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ["22.x", "24.x"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        if: matrix.node == '22.x'
        with:
          name: ts-build
          path: out/
          retention-days: 7

  # v1.18.0 Phase 7: the three-OS sandbox matrix lives in
  # .github/workflows/sandbox.yml (path-filtered). PRs still cover those
  # files via this workflow's ubuntu test-ts job.
  #
  # v1.19.0 Phase 4: installer pytest + headless-smoke moved to
  # .github/workflows/installer-tests.yml (path-filtered to
  # scripts/installer + core/registry). Unrelated pushes skip PyQt/uv.

  # ── Module catalog sync check ─────────────────────────────────────────────

  catalog-sync:
    name: docs/index.md sync check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - name: Regenerate module catalog
        run: node scripts/generate-catalog.mjs
      - name: Diff committed vs regenerated
        run: |
          if ! git diff --exit-code docs/index.md; then
            echo ""
            echo "docs/index.md is out of sync with src/."
            echo "Run \`npm run catalog\` and commit the regenerated file."
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Safety-surface SSOT drift gate (perm tiers + egress denylist + secret paths)
        run: npm run security:check

  # ── Coverage gate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  coverage-gate:
    name: Coverage gate (80%)
    needs: [test-ts]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: ts-coverage
          path: coverage/

      - name: Check TypeScript coverage threshold
        # Reads coverage-summary.json (structured data) instead of scraping
        # the lcov-report HTML with a regex. jq + awk is portable, single
        # tool installation, and resilient to formatter changes upstream.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          summary=coverage/coverage-summary.json
          if [ ! -f "$summary" ]; then
            echo "Missing $summary -- the test job must emit the json-summary reporter."
            exit 1
          fi
          lines=$(jq -r '.total.lines.pct' "$summary")
          branches=$(jq -r '.total.branches.pct' "$summary")
          functions=$(jq -r '.total.functions.pct' "$summary")
          printf 'TS line coverage:     %s%%\n' "$lines"
          printf 'TS branch coverage:   %s%%\n' "$branches"
          printf 'TS function coverage: %s%%\n' "$functions"
          awk -v v="$lines"     'BEGIN { exit (v + 0 < 80) }' || { echo "TS line coverage $lines% is below the 80% threshold"; exit 1; }
          awk -v v="$branches"  'BEGIN { exit (v + 0 < 75) }' || { echo "TS branch coverage $branches% is below the 75% threshold"; exit 1; }
          awk -v v="$functions" 'BEGIN { exit (v + 0 < 80) }' || { echo "TS function coverage $functions% is below the 80% threshold"; exit 1; }
          echo "TS coverage gates: OK"

  # -- nexus-check self-scan (v1.0.0; renamed from gemma-check in Phase 2.4) -
  #
  # Runs the standalone deterministic-checks CLI across the repository. The
  # exact-count baseline accepts only reviewed historical fixtures; new,
  # excess, or stale error findings fail. The CLI is LLM-free and the gate is
  # "no unbaselined error-severity findings".
  #
  # v0.8.0 Phase 7 (post-CI): warnings (e.g. prompt-oversized) emit to
  # stdout for visibility but do not flip the exit code. Run `--strict` to
  # restore the legacy "any finding fails" behaviour (use only in
  # zero-tolerance gates -- not the default for this surface).

  nexus-check:
    name: nexus-check (repository)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - run: npm run check
      # v1.4.0 Phase 3 (A2) -- test-tampering rules over tests/ and the CI
      # workflows themselves. nexus-check is dependency-free, so this needs no
      # `npm ci`. Error-severity rules (no-focused-tests,
      # no-tautological-assertion) gate the merge; the rest emit warnings.
      - name: nexus-check (test-tampering rules)
        run: npm run check:tampering
      # v1.10.0 Phase 7 (T039) -- naming gate: fail if the load-bearing
      # "devai-hub" enum value (renamed to "nexus-hub" in v1.10.0) reappears in
      # source. Dependency-free (node:fs / node:path only), so no npm ci.
      - name: naming gate (no devai-hub enum value)
        run: npm run check:naming
      # v1.10.0 Phase 8 (T048) -- docs-layout gate: fail if the retired
      # docs/versions or docs/archive/versions wrappers reappear (canonical
      # layout is docs/v<MAJOR>/v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>/). Dependency-free, no npm ci.
      - name: docs-layout gate (canonical version dirs)
        run: npm run check:docs-layout

  # -- v0.9.0 Phase 7 (sub-task 7.5) -- PR-time fast-bench gate --------------
  #
  # Runs ONLY the MarkdownRenderer benches (`render ~*-token message`) on every
  # push so a rendering perf regression is caught at PR time rather than next
  # day in `nightly.yml`. The full benchmark suite (eviction, memory, hooks,
  # tool execution, golden tasks) still runs nightly because those benches are
  # slower, noisier on shared runners, or require Ollama.
  fast-bench:
    name: fast-bench (rendering)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - run: npm run build
      - name: Run rendering benches
        # `-t render` matches the three `render ~*-token message` bench names.
        # The custom JSON reporter (`scripts/vitest-bench-json-reporter.mjs`)
        # mirrors what `nightly.yml` uses because Vitest 1.x bench mode lacks a
        # built-in JSON reporter.
        run: npm run bench -- -t render --reporter=verbose --reporter=./scripts/vitest-bench-json-reporter.mjs --outputFile=bench-results.json 2>&1 | tee bench-results.txt
      - name: Check rendering bench regressions
        run: |
          node scripts/check-bench-regressions.mjs \
            --baseline tests/benchmarks/baselines/v0.7.0.json \
            --current bench-results.json \
            --regression-pct 20 \
            --fail-on-regression
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        if: always()
        with:
          name: fast-bench-results
          path: |
            bench-results.txt
            bench-results.json
          retention-days: 14

  # -- v0.9.0 Phase 7 (sub-task 7.3) -- dedicated prompt-quality gate -------
  #
  # `npm run check:prompts` runs the prompt-specific lint rules
  # (prompt-no-ascii-violation, prompt-oversized, prompt-trailing-whitespace,
  # prompt-bom, skill-duplicate-name) against the chat prompts and the skill
  # catalog. A separate job keeps a regressing prompt-asset PR distinct from
  # general gemma-check noise: when this job fails, the diff lives in the
  # prompts surface, which is high-value and small.
  check-prompts:
    name: check-prompts
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - run: npm run check:prompts

  # -- VSIX packaging smoke check (v0.8.0 Phase 7 post-CI audit) ------------
  #
  # The extension ships as a `.vsix` produced by the canonical build script.
  # Building it on every push catches `files`/`.vscodeignore` drift, missing
  # assets, and native modules built for Node instead of VS Code Electron.
  # The produced VSIX is uploaded as a 7-day artifact so a reviewer can pull
  # it down and load it into VS Code to verify the install path manually.

  package-vsix:
    name: Package VSIX (smoke)
    needs: [build-ts]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - name: Build VSIX with Electron native modules
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./scripts/build-vsix.ps1 -SkipTests
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: vsix-smoke
          path: nexus-coding-*.vsix
          retention-days: 7

  # -- v0.8.0 Phase 6.5 (item C6) -------------------------------------------
  # Architecture boundary check via dependency-cruiser. Fails fast on any
  # violation; re-run `bash scripts/check-architecture.sh --verbose` to inspect.

  # v2.4.9 Phase 3 -- the feature inventory has to stay true. feature_list.json
  # claimed v0.8.0 against a product shipping 2.4.x and no job read it, which is
  # how an inventory becomes decoration. This gates it in both directions: every
  # evidence path must resolve, and the inventory and the two README regions must
  # name the same features. No npm install needed -- the checker is dependency-free.
  check-feature-drift:
    name: check-feature-drift
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - run: node scripts/check-feature-drift.mjs

  # v2.5.1 Phase 2: command parity. Not path-scoped. A skipped path-filtered
  # job is treated as green by branch protection, and the commit that adds a
  # command in a new file is exactly the commit this gate has to see.
  check-command-parity:
    name: check-command-parity
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - run: node scripts/check-command-parity.mjs
      - run: node scripts/ci-profile.mjs --profile fast --list --json
      - run: node scripts/ci-profile.mjs --profile full --list --json
      - run: node scripts/ci-profile.mjs --profile platform --list --json
      - run: node scripts/ci-profile.mjs --profile report --list --json
      - run: node scripts/ci-profile.mjs --profile release --list --json

  check-release-assets:
    name: check-release-assets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - run: node scripts/check-release-assets.mjs

  check-architecture:
    name: check-architecture
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      # v0.9.0 Phase 7 (sub-task 7.6) -- Graphviz is required for
      # `npm run deps:graph` (depcruise pipes DOT through `dot -Tsvg`).
      - name: Install graphviz
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends graphviz
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - run: bash scripts/check-architecture.sh
      # v0.9.0 Phase 7 (sub-task 7.6) -- regenerate and publish the dep graph
      # as a 7-day artifact so reviewers can download the post-refactor SVG
      # without re-running depcruise locally.
      - name: Regenerate dependency graph SVG
        run: npm run deps:graph
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: dep-graph-svg
          path: docs/archive/v0/v0.5/dep-graph.svg
          retention-days: 7

  # -- v0.8.0 Phase 2 (item C2) ---------------------------------------------
  # Lifecycle bootstrap must exit 0 on Linux/macOS (init.sh) and Windows
  # (init.ps1). Five verified steps before any work begins: install, lint,
  # build, harness-files check, specialist-assets check.

  init-check-posix:
    name: init.sh (Linux)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: bash scripts/init.sh

  init-check-windows:
    name: init.ps1 (Windows)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    # Cost control: Windows is a 2x-minute runner. Validate the PowerShell
    # bootstrap on push to main only, not on every PR (init.sh covers Linux on PRs).
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: pwsh -File scripts/init.ps1
        shell: pwsh

  # -- Python runtime tests --------------------------------------------------
  #
  # v1.16.0 Phase 3 (adoption item A5). `tests/python/` had NO CI job at all:
  # the ~135 diffusion-runtime tests added in v1.0.0 Phase 6 have only ever been
  # run by hand. Adding the OCR runtime made that gap load-bearing, so this job
  # covers diffusion, OCR, (v2.0.0 Phase 1) the audio STT/TTS stub, and
  # (v2.1.0 Phase 5) the Unsloth train.py --stub path, and (v2.1.0 Phase 6)
  # diffusion budget + layer-streaming rescue (no GPU weights).
  #
  # No GPU, no model weights, and no CUDA stack: the runtimes import every heavy
  # dependency lazily and ship stub engines, so `health`, `version`, the
  # dispatcher, the error envelopes, the PDF path, native Office ingest, and
  # audio STT/TTS stubs are exercised on a bare runner. Portable OCR + Office
  # wheels come from `runtimes/ocr/requirements.txt` (pypdfium2,
  # rapidocr-onnxruntime, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl). Audio tests do
  # not install faster-whisper or Kokoro (`NEXUS_AUDIO_STUB=1` plus health
  # without engines). torch/transformers and docling are deliberately NOT
  # installed.

  test-python-runtimes:
    name: pytest (runtimes/)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: "pip"
      - name: Install portable runtime deps (no torch, no GPU)
        run: |
          python -m pip install --quiet --upgrade pip
          python -m pip install --quiet pytest
          python -m pip install --quiet -r runtimes/ocr/requirements.txt
      - name: Run runtime tests
        run: python -m pytest tests/python -q
        env:
          NEXUS_AUDIO_STUB: "1"

  # -- Dependency audits ----------------------------------------------------
  #
  # Gate on known CVEs for both the TypeScript extension and the PyQt5
  # installer. `npm audit` runs against production-only deps; `pip-audit`
  # targets the installer venv (only remaining Python surface after ADR-0001).

  audit-ts:
    name: npm audit (production deps)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      # v1.2.0 cycle close -- the bare `npm audit --omit=dev` fails on a
      # documented transitive CVE chain (`@xenova/transformers` ->
      # `onnxruntime-web` -> `onnx-proto` -> `protobufjs`) inherited from
      # the v1.1.0 Phase 5 local-embedder shipment. The chain cannot be
      # fixed without a semver-major dependency move (tracked as
      # `docs/archive/v1/v1.2/known-gaps.md` entry 7.x.P1.D). The
      # allowlist script below filters that chain by name and fails only
      # on NEW non-allowlisted advisories at severity >= moderate.
      - name: npm audit (production deps, allowlisted)
        run: npm run check:audit-prod

  # Visibility-only audit covering both prod and dev dependencies. Captures
  # the full CVE picture (including build/test toolchain) without gating the
  # merge -- runs with continue-on-error so a new dev-dep CVE never blocks a
  # release. Artifact retention lets us spot drift over time.
  audit-ts-dev:
    name: npm audit (dev + prod, non-blocking)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true # nexus-check-allow: no-disabled-ci-check -- visibility-only dev+prod audit; intentionally never gates a merge (see job comment above)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
      - name: npm audit --audit-level=high (json)
        continue-on-error: true # nexus-check-allow: no-disabled-ci-check -- non-gating JSON capture for the uploaded artifact; failure is tolerated by design
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high --json > audit-dev.json || true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        if: always()
        with:
          name: audit-dev
          path: audit-dev.json
          retention-days: 30

  audit-py:
    name: pip-audit (installer venv)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@e4db8464a088ece1b920f60402e813ea4de65b8f # v4
        with:
          version: "latest"
      - name: Cache pip-audit advisory DB
        uses: actions/cache@27d5ce7f107fe9357f9df03efb73ab90386fccae # v5.0.5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip-audit
          key: pip-audit-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('scripts/installer/uv.lock') }}
      - name: Export installer dependencies to requirements-audit.txt
        # `--no-emit-project` excludes the local `gemma-code-installer` package
        # from the audited set; pip-audit cannot look up an unpublished package.
        run: |
          cd scripts/installer
          uv export \
            --no-hashes \
            --no-annotate \
            --format requirements-txt \
            --no-emit-project \
            > requirements-audit.txt
      - name: Run pip-audit
        run: |
          cd scripts/installer
          uv run --with pip-audit -- pip-audit --strict -r requirements-audit.txt

  # v2.4.9 Phase 2 -- the three requirement sets that actually reach a user
  # machine. A SIBLING job, deliberately not a matrix dimension on audit-py:
  # that job is built around a uv project (its cache key is the installer's
  # uv.lock and it runs `uv export`), and the runtime sets are plain
  # requirements.txt with no lock file, so neither the key nor the export
  # transfers.
  #
  # Resolution strategy, decided in Phase 2 and stated here because it changes
  # what the numbers mean: the runtime sets are audited RESOLVED, not as
  # written. They carry no exact pins at all (runtimes/diffusion pins nothing;
  # the other two carry only `>=` floors), so "as written" has no version to
  # check an advisory against. Resolving is also what matches a user machine,
  # where the installer builds the venv from wheels resolved at payload-build
  # time. pip-audit resolves each requirement to the latest matching version,
  # which is what a fresh install gets.
  #
  # Naming note: the existing installer job above deliberately keeps its
  # original check name. Renaming it would churn a name that branch protection
  # references, for cosmetic gain, which is the same footgun this plan flagged
  # for the CodeQL check. This job is unambiguous on its own instead.
  #
  # D2 (answered 2026-09-10) made this GATING, on the strength of the
  # measurement rather than a preference: all three sets resolve to 180
  # packages with ZERO advisories today, so gating costs nothing now and any
  # red is new information.
  #
  # The failure mode the plan worried about is real and is handled explicitly
  # below: an unfixable upstream ML advisory must not block every merge
  # forever. When one lands, add it to IGNORE_VULNS with a dated reason rather
  # than turning the job off.
  audit-runtimes:
    name: pip-audit (model runtimes)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Cache pip-audit advisory DB
        uses: actions/cache@27d5ce7f107fe9357f9df03efb73ab90386fccae # v5.0.5
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip-audit
          key: pip-audit-runtimes-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('runtimes/*/requirements.txt') }}
      - name: Install pip-audit
        run: python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check pip-audit
      - name: Audit each runtime requirement set
        # Fails loudly on a missing or unparseable file, naming it, rather than
        # skipping it silently. Advisory findings are reported, not gated.
        run: |
          set -u
          status=0
          # Unfixable upstream advisories go here with a dated reason, so one
          # of them cannot hold every merge hostage. Empty today.
          IGNORE_VULNS=""
          IGNORE_ARGS=""
          for vuln in $IGNORE_VULNS; do
            IGNORE_ARGS="$IGNORE_ARGS --ignore-vuln $vuln"
          done
          for set_name in audio diffusion ocr; do
            req="runtimes/${set_name}/requirements.txt"
            if [ ! -f "$req" ]; then
              echo "::error file=${req}::runtime requirement set is missing"
              status=1
              continue
            fi
            echo "::group::pip-audit ${req}"
            if ! python -m pip_audit -r "$req" --progress-spinner off                  ${IGNORE_ARGS}                  --format json --output "audit-${set_name}.json"; then
              echo "::error file=${req}::pip-audit reported advisories for ${set_name}"
              status=1
            fi
            python - "$set_name" <<'PYCOUNT'
          import json, sys
          name = sys.argv[1]
          with open(f"audit-{name}.json", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
              report = json.load(fh)
          deps = report.get("dependencies", [])
          flagged = [d for d in deps if d.get("vulns")]
          print(f"{name}: {len(deps)} packages audited, {len(flagged)} with advisories")
          for dep in flagged:
              ids = ", ".join(v.get("id", "?") for v in dep["vulns"])
              print(f"  - {dep['name']} {dep.get('version')}: {ids}")
          PYCOUNT
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          exit "$status"
      - name: Upload runtime audit reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: audit-runtimes
          path: audit-*.json
          retention-days: 30

  # One always-resolving aggregate. Branch protection should require this
  # context rather than a per-job or per-matrix-leg name. Skipped is allowed
  # because a job-level condition reports success-by-skip; every other result
  # fails closed.
  ci-required:
    name: ci-required
    needs:
      - lint-ts
      - test-ts
      - build-ts
      - catalog-sync
      - coverage-gate
      - nexus-check
      - fast-bench
      - check-prompts
      - package-vsix
      - check-feature-drift
      - check-command-parity
      - check-release-assets
      - check-architecture
      - init-check-posix
      - init-check-windows
      - test-python-runtimes
      - audit-ts
      - audit-ts-dev
      - audit-py
      - audit-runtimes
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Allowlist job results
        env:
          R_lint_ts: ${{ needs.lint-ts.result }}
          R_test_ts: ${{ needs.test-ts.result }}
          R_build_ts: ${{ needs.build-ts.result }}
          R_catalog_sync: ${{ needs.catalog-sync.result }}
          R_coverage_gate: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_nexus_check: ${{ needs.nexus-check.result }}
          R_fast_bench: ${{ needs.fast-bench.result }}
          R_check_prompts: ${{ needs.check-prompts.result }}
          R_package_vsix: ${{ needs.package-vsix.result }}
          R_check_feature_drift: ${{ needs.check-feature-drift.result }}
          R_check_command_parity: ${{ needs.check-command-parity.result }}
          R_check_release_assets: ${{ needs.check-release-assets.result }}
          R_check_architecture: ${{ needs.check-architecture.result }}
          R_init_check_posix: ${{ needs.init-check-posix.result }}
          R_init_check_windows: ${{ needs.init-check-windows.result }}
          R_test_python_runtimes: ${{ needs.test-python-runtimes.result }}
          R_audit_ts: ${{ needs.audit-ts.result }}
          R_audit_ts_dev: ${{ needs.audit-ts-dev.result }}
          R_audit_py: ${{ needs.audit-py.result }}
          R_audit_runtimes: ${{ needs.audit-runtimes.result }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          fail=0
          for var in $(env | sed -n 's/^\(R_[A-Za-z0-9_]*\)=.*/\1/p' | sort); do
            eval "result=\${${var}-}"
            case "${result}" in
              success|skipped) ;;
              *) echo "FAIL: ${var#R_}=${result:-<empty>}"; fail=1 ;;
            esac
          done
          exit "$fail"

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"
  # Rebuild and attach assets to an existing tag only when the selected ref
  # resolves to that exact tagged commit. This prevents attaching assets built
  # from different code to an older release.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag_name:
        description: "Existing tag to attach assets to (e.g. v1.19.0)"
        required: true
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.tag_name || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:

  # -- Validate release identity ----------------------------------------------

  release-metadata:
    name: Validate release metadata
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.version }}
      tag_name: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.tag_name }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      - name: Match package version, tag, and checked-out commit
        id: metadata
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.tag_name || github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          EXPECTED_TAG="v${VERSION}"
          if [ "$RELEASE_TAG" != "$EXPECTED_TAG" ]; then
            echo "Release tag $RELEASE_TAG does not match package version $EXPECTED_TAG" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          git fetch --force --tags origin
          TAG_SHA=$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}^{commit}")
          CURRENT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
          if [ "$TAG_SHA" != "$CURRENT_SHA" ] || [ "$TAG_SHA" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Release tag $RELEASE_TAG does not resolve to the checked-out workflow commit" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "tag_name=$RELEASE_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # -- Re-run the release gate on the tagged commit ---------------------------

  release-verification:
    name: Verify release source
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-metadata
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Install workspace dependencies
        run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit

      - name: Lint extension source
        run: npm run lint --silent

      - name: Test extension source
        run: npm run test --silent

      - name: Build extension source
        run: npm run build --silent

  # -- Build native VSIX packages (3-OS) --------------------------------------

  build-vsix:
    name: Build VSIX (${{ matrix.platform }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [release-metadata, release-verification]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: windows
            os: windows-latest
            vsce_os: win32
            vsce_arch: x64
          - platform: macos
            os: macos-15
            vsce_os: darwin
            vsce_arch: arm64
          - platform: linux
            # Build the native VSIX on Ubuntu 22.04 so its glibc floor stays
            # at the documented 2.35 baseline.
            os: ubuntu-22.04
            vsce_os: linux
            vsce_arch: x64
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Build and package VSIX for VS Code Electron
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $HostArch = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture.ToString().ToLowerInvariant()
          $ExpectedArch = "${{ matrix.vsce_arch }}"
          if ($HostArch -ne $ExpectedArch) {
            throw "Runner architecture mismatch for ${{ matrix.platform }}: expected $ExpectedArch, found $HostArch"
          }
          $Target = "${{ matrix.vsce_os }}-$ExpectedArch"
          ./scripts/build-vsix.ps1 -SkipTests -Target $Target
          $Vsix = "nexus-coding-${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}-$Target.vsix"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Vsix)) {
            throw "Expected VSIX was not produced: $Vsix"
          }

      - name: Smoke-test packaged VSIX on VS Code 1.134.0
        if: matrix.platform == 'windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: npm run test:vsix-runtime -- --vsix "nexus-coding-${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}-win32-x64.vsix"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: vsix-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: nexus-coding-${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}-${{ matrix.vsce_os }}-*.vsix
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

  # -- Build Windows installer (PyQt5) ----------------------------------------

  build-installer-windows:
    name: Build Windows installer
    runs-on: windows-latest
    # The wizard embeds the Tauri NSIS bundle (v1.11.0 T401, fail-closed).
    # That file is produced by desktop-bundle, not by this job, so wait
    # for the Windows matrix leg's artifact rather than racing it.
    needs: [build-vsix, desktop-bundle]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@a309ff8b426b58ec0e2a45f0f869d46889d02405 # v6.2.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@e4db8464a088ece1b920f60402e813ea4de65b8f # v4
        with:
          version: "latest"

      - name: Download VSIX artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: vsix-windows
          path: .

      - name: Download Windows desktop bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: desktop-bundle-windows
          path: desktop-bundle-windows

      - name: Build installer
        run: pwsh -NonInteractive -File scripts/installer/build/build-windows.ps1 -SkipSign

      - name: Smoke-test the installer
        shell: pwsh
        run: pwsh -NonInteractive -File scripts/installer/build/smoke-windows-exe.ps1

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: installer-windows
          path: dist/NexusSetup.exe
          retention-days: 30

  # -- Build the private Windows desktop payload -------------------------------
  #
  # The complete Windows wizard embeds this matching Tauri bundle. Raw Tauri
  # bundles are not v2.2.9 release assets because they do not carry the pinned
  # Node runtime and runtime manifest supplied by the provisioning installer.
  # tauri.conf.json's version is synced from package.json at build time.

  desktop-bundle:
    name: Windows desktop payload (installer input)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    needs: [release-metadata, release-verification]
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8 # stable

      - name: Cache cargo registry + target
        uses: actions/cache@27d5ce7f107fe9357f9df03efb73ab90386fccae # v5.0.5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: windows-desktop-payload-cargo-${{ hashFiles('desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            windows-desktop-payload-cargo-

      - name: Install workspace deps
        run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit

      - name: Sync tauri.conf.json version from package.json
        run: node scripts/sync-tauri-version.mjs

      - name: Remove cached Tauri bundle outputs
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $RepoRoot = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.').Path
          $BundleDirs = @(
            'desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle',
            'desktop/src-tauri/target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle'
          )
          foreach ($RelativePath in $BundleDirs) {
            $Candidate = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $RepoRoot $RelativePath))
            $WorkspacePrefix = $RepoRoot.TrimEnd([System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar, [System.IO.Path]::AltDirectorySeparatorChar) + [System.IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar
            if (-not $Candidate.StartsWith($WorkspacePrefix, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {
              throw "Refusing to remove bundle path outside the workspace: $Candidate"
            }
            if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Candidate) {
              Remove-Item -LiteralPath $Candidate -Recurse -Force
            }
          }

      - name: Build sidecar bundle (fail-fast)
        working-directory: desktop
        run: npm run build:sidecar

      - name: Build Windows Tauri payload
        working-directory: desktop
        run: npm run build:shell

      - name: Probe the shell that this payload embeds
        working-directory: desktop
        shell: cmd
        run: node tests/packaged/launch-probe.mjs src-tauri/target/release/nexus-shell.exe > ..\shell-smoke.json

      - name: Stage current Windows payload
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $v = "${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}"
          $BundleDir = "desktop/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis"
          $Matches = @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $BundleDir -Filter "Nexus AI Studio_${v}_x64-setup.exe" -File)
          if ($Matches.Count -ne 1) {
            throw "Expected exactly one Windows desktop bundle for version $v; found $($Matches.Count)"
          }
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force bundle-out | Out-Null
          Copy-Item -LiteralPath $Matches[0].FullName "bundle-out/Nexus-Desktop_${v}_x64-setup.exe"
          $smokePath = "shell-smoke.json"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $smokePath)) {
            throw "shell smoke report is missing"
          }
          $smoke = Get-Content -Raw -LiteralPath $smokePath | ConvertFrom-Json
          if ($smoke.ok -ne $true) {
            throw "shell smoke did not pass"
          }
          Copy-Item -LiteralPath $smokePath "bundle-out/shell-smoke.json"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: desktop-bundle-windows
          path: bundle-out/*
          retention-days: 30

  # -- Create GitHub Release ---------------------------------------------------

  create-release:
    name: Create GitHub Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-metadata, release-verification, build-vsix, build-installer-windows]
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: vsix-windows
          path: artifacts/

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: vsix-macos
          path: artifacts/

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: vsix-linux
          path: artifacts/

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: installer-windows
          path: artifacts/

      # One SHA256SUMS.txt covers every attached binary. The explicit list
      # fails closed if a platform VSIX or the complete Windows installer is
      # missing, and deliberately excludes raw Tauri bundles.
      - name: Generate SHA256SUMS.txt
        run: |
          VERSION="${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}"
          cd artifacts
          shopt -s nullglob
          VSIX_FILES=(nexus-coding-${VERSION}-*.vsix)
          if [ ${#VSIX_FILES[@]} -ne 3 ]; then
            echo "Expected 3 platform-specific VSIX files, found ${#VSIX_FILES[@]}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          sha256sum \
            "${VSIX_FILES[@]}" \
            NexusSetup.exe \
            > SHA256SUMS.txt
          cat SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Extract release notes from CHANGELOG
        id: changelog
        run: |
          VERSION="${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}"
          NOTES=$(awk -v version="$VERSION" '
            index($0, "# [" version "]") == 1 { flag=1; next }
            flag && /^# / { exit }
            flag { print }
          ' CHANGELOG.md)
          echo "notes<<EOF" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "$NOTES" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "EOF" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Revalidate annotated tag immediately before publication
        env:
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.tag_name }}
          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          REMOTE_TAGS=$(git ls-remote --tags origin "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}" "refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}^{}")
          TAG_SHA=$(printf '%s\n' "$REMOTE_TAGS" | awk '$2 ~ /\^\{\}$/ {print $1; exit}')
          if [ -z "$TAG_SHA" ]; then
            TAG_SHA=$(printf '%s\n' "$REMOTE_TAGS" | awk -v tag="refs/tags/${RELEASE_TAG}" '$2 == tag {print $1; exit}')
          fi
          if [ -z "$TAG_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Annotated release tag ${RELEASE_TAG} is missing or has no peeled commit on origin" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$TAG_SHA" != "$EXPECTED_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Release tag ${RELEASE_TAG} moved during the workflow: expected ${EXPECTED_SHA}, found ${TAG_SHA}" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Create release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@da05d552573ad5aba039eaac05058a918a7bf631 # v2.2.2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.tag_name }}
          target_commitish: ${{ github.sha }}
          name: "Nexus v${{ needs.release-metadata.outputs.version }}"
          body: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.notes }}
          draft: false
          prerelease: ${{ contains(needs.release-metadata.outputs.tag_name, '-') }}
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          files: |
            artifacts/nexus-coding-*.vsix
            artifacts/NexusSetup.exe
            artifacts/SHA256SUMS.txt

name: Shell Build (Tauri + Vite)

on:
  # v1.16.0 Phase 1 (adoption item A1): `modules/**` joined the filter because the
  # sidecar bundle imports from it (the serving gateway pulls the vscode-free
  # `modules/coding/llm/loopback.ts` + `headlessOpenAiClient.ts`, and `main.ts`
  # has long pulled `headlessOllamaClient.ts`). Without it a module-only change
  # could break `build:sidecar` with no shell build to catch it. Cost stays
  # bounded: PRs and develop pushes run ubuntu-only, and the macOS (10x) +
  # Windows (2x) matrix is still gated to push-to-main or manual dispatch.
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
    paths:
      - "desktop/**"
      - "core/**"
      - "modules/**"
      - ".github/workflows/shell-build.yml"
  pull_request:
    # v2.4.4 Phase 7 (QG-5): `develop` joined this list because the
    # integration pull request targets it. Without it a develop-targeted
    # PR ran only commitlint, so the branch head was tested by the push
    # trigger but the MERGE RESULT -- the thing that actually ships --
    # never was. Path filters already keep the added cost bounded.
    branches: [main, develop]
    paths:
      - "desktop/**"
      - "core/**"
      - "modules/**"
      - ".github/workflows/shell-build.yml"
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  group: shell-build-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  shell:
    name: "Shell ${{ matrix.os }}"
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Cost control: PRs and develop pushes run ubuntu-only (fast,
        # platform-agnostic gate). The full macOS (10x) + Windows (2x) matrix
        # runs on push-to-main and manual dispatch, where release-representative
        # builds matter.
        os: ${{ (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && fromJSON('["windows-latest","macos-latest","ubuntu-latest"]') || fromJSON('["ubuntu-latest"]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: desktop
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1

      - uses: actions/setup-node@a0853c24544627f65ddf259abe73b1d18a591444 # v5.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22.x"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json

      - name: Install Linux Tauri prerequisites
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@29eef336d9b2848a0b548edc03f92a220660cdb8 # stable

      - name: Cache cargo registry + target
        uses: actions/cache@27d5ce7f107fe9357f9df03efb73ab90386fccae # v5.0.5
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            desktop/src-tauri/target
          key: ${{ matrix.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ matrix.os }}-cargo-

      - name: Install workspace deps
        working-directory: .
        run: npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit

      - name: Lint frontend
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck frontend
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Build sidecar bundle
        run: npm run build:sidecar

      - name: Vitest (frontend + sidecar) with coverage
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Cargo check (Tauri core)
        working-directory: desktop/src-tauri
        run: cargo check --all-targets

      - name: Cargo clippy (Tauri core)
        working-directory: desktop/src-tauri
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo test (Tauri core)
        working-directory: desktop/src-tauri
        run: cargo test --all-targets
        # v2.2.8 Phase 6: cargo test covers rpc_timeout_for (T001: chat.send /
        # generate minutes-class; ping stays 15s). No live GPU.

      - name: Build frontend bundle
        run: npm run build:web

      - name: Upload coverage
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: shell-coverage
          path: desktop/coverage
          if-no-files-found: ignore

name: Scorecard

# v1.4.0 Phase 3 (sub-task 3.2, A2/A9) -- OpenSSF Scorecard supply-chain
# posture scan, sitting alongside the CodeQL SAST workflow (codeql.yml).
# Scorecard scores repository hygiene (branch protection, pinned actions,
# token permissions, dangerous workflow patterns, dependency-update tooling,
# ...) and uploads SARIF to the GitHub Security tab so findings are triaged in
# the same place as CodeQL. Runs weekly plus on push to the default branch and
# on branch-protection changes (which can affect the score directly).
#
# All actions are pinned by full commit SHA per the repo's SHA-pin policy;
# the trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment records the human-readable tag.

# Gated to manual dispatch only. This repo is PRIVATE, and OpenSSF Scorecard is
# designed for PUBLIC repositories: its checkout runs with `persist-credentials:
# false` and cannot authenticate to a private repo (checkout fails with
# "Repository not found"), while `publish_results: true` targets the public
# OpenSSF API. The automatic push / schedule / branch-protection triggers
# therefore failed on every run. Re-enable them (and revisit publish_results) if
# this repository is ever made public.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: scorecard-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Top-level least privilege; the analysis job widens only what it needs.
permissions: read-all

jobs:
  analysis:
    name: Scorecard analysis
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      # Needed to upload the SARIF results to the code-scanning dashboard.
      security-events: write
      # Needed by the publish_results step to attach the signed result.
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: "Checkout code"
        uses: actions/checkout@93cb6efe18208431cddfb8368fd83d5badbf9bfd # v5.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: "Run analysis"
        uses: ossf/scorecard-action@4eaacf0543bb3f2c246792bd56e8cdeffafb205a # v2.4.3
        with:
          results_file: results.sarif
          results_format: sarif
          # publish_results sends the score to the public OpenSSF API so the
          # repo can display a Scorecard badge; results are public for public
          # repos regardless, and no source is uploaded.
          publish_results: true

      # Upload the raw SARIF as a build artifact for offline inspection.
      - name: "Upload artifact"
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@330a01c490aca151604b8cf639adc76d48f6c5d4 # v5.0.0
        with:
          name: scorecard-sarif
          path: results.sarif
          retention-days: 7

      # Upload to the GitHub code-scanning dashboard (same surface as CodeQL).
      - name: "Upload to code-scanning"
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@f411752efdf656cb71aa17b755b22c890960da1d # v3.35.5
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif
